source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib path-law transport supplement: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost
source_evidence.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). For every fixed \(s\in T\), the Kantorovich cost with cost \(c\) from \(\mu_t\) to \(\mu_s\) tends to zero as \(t\to s\). The limit is in the extended nonnegative reals.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
source_evidence.boundary: The cost need not be a metric or symmetric. Compactness and the finite continuous cost are retained. This is a limit at each fixed time, without a quantitative rate.

definition_semantics.couplingSet: Exactly the set of measures satisfying IsCoupling.
definition_semantics.transportCost: sInf of the set of extended-nonnegative integrals of the supplied cost over feasible couplings; no optimizer or existence premise is built into the definition.
definition_semantics.probability_coupling_equivalence: Every feasible measure here has mass one because its first marginal is a probability measure.
definition_semantics.nonempty_feasible_set: The same-sample joint pushforward is an explicit feasible coupling.
definition_semantics.finite_cost_bridge: On compact E×E, continuous finite c is bounded and measurable. Its coupling integrals, and those of c², are finite. This is derived, not an extra premise.
definition_semantics.operator_order: Coerce c from NNReal to ENNReal before the nonnegative integral.

steps.title: Use the same sample at two times
steps.text: The paired process \(Z_t=(X_t,X_s)\) has continuous sample paths on the original full event. The marginal-law theorem therefore makes \(\gamma_t=(Z_t)_\#P\) weakly continuous. Its two marginals are \(\mu_t,\mu_s\).
steps.assessment: The stated move matches the actual proof and its scope; all required assumptions are already in the public statement or derived internally.

steps.title: Integrate the continuous cost
steps.text: Compactness bounds the continuous cost, and the measurable-open-set assumption makes it measurable. Its integral is continuous in the probability law. At \(s\), both coordinates coincide, so this cost integral is zero.
steps.assessment: The stated move matches the actual proof and its scope; all required assumptions are already in the public statement or derived internally.

steps.title: Bound the infimum by this coupling
steps.text: The transport cost is nonnegative and at most the cost of the explicit coupling. Squeezing gives the asserted limit.
